title: Experiment fallout mapping and rollback choreography (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for mapping the possible "fallout" (observable customer-facing degradations) from cross-functional experiments (canaries / A-Bs / microreleases) to explicit rollback choreography. Aim: reduce decision time during incidents by having pre-mapped actions, owners, and automated playbooks for common and plausible failure modes.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus on user-visible fallout for LLM-powered features (generation/chat, reranking, embeddings-backed search).
- Covers staged and cohorted rollouts where traffic slices route to new model or prompt pipeline variation.
- Assumes instrumentation for: latency p50/p95/p99, token-level error flags, safety checks (policy hits), semantic-drift score (eval-based), user satisfaction proxy (post-interaction rating), cost-per-token by route.
- Not covering infra-level outages (GPU node failures) — those are SRE-run. This doc maps experiment-specific degradations and stepped rollbacks.

Quick taxonomy of fallout (operator-facing names):
1) Latency inflation: sustained p95 > baseline + X ms across slice for Y minutes. Feels like slow responses / degraded UX.
2) Quality regression: drop in automated eval pass rate (eval-suite) or drop in user satisfaction proxy by >Z%.
3) Safety regression: increase in policy hits / safety flag rate above threshold.
4) Semantic drift: model outputs off-domain or hallucinating (signal from targeted evals + customer reports).
5) Cost runaway: cost-per-token or allocation consumption > budget multiple.
6) Distribution oscillation / instability: A-B causing high variance in returns or repeatable flakiness (often intermittent).
7) Silent failure: increase in HTTP 5xx or partial responses / truncated tokens.
8) Unintended feature interaction: new channel triggers downstream components (e.g., reranker exposure causing cascade).

Fallout -> detection signals -> example thresholds (work in progress):
- Latency inflation -> latency.p95_experiment / latency.p95_baseline; threshold: > baseline + 250ms for 10m window OR sustained 2x baseline for 5m.
- Quality regression -> eval.pass_rate delta <= -3% over rolling 1k requests; user_rating delta <= -5% over 30m.
- Safety regression -> safety.flag_rate_experiment >= baseline * 3 OR absolute rate > 0.5% for high-risk cohorts.
- Semantic drift -> semantic_similarity_to_reference drop > 0.08 average on targeted prompts.
- Cost runaway -> cost_per_token_experiment > baseline * 2 for 15m or projected burn exceeds reserved pool by 10% in next hour.
- Silent failure -> http_5xx > 0.5% or truncated_response_rate > 0.2% in 10m window.

Decision ladder / rollback choreography (automation + human gates):
Level 0 — Soft mitigations (fast, reversible, low blast radius):
- Action: Route experiment slices to baseline model for new requests; allow in-flight sessions to finish with variant if safe.
- Trigger: latency.p95 threshold OR small quality blip.
- Automation: console button + API call (route_override: baseline) + ticket auto-populated.
- Owner: Release steward (product eng) + oncall ENG.

Level 1 — Canary throttle and patch (temporary reduction):
- Action: Reduce exposure fraction by 80% (e.g., from 10% -> 2%) or move from 10% global to synthetic traffic only.
- Trigger: persistent signals across multiple cohorts or mixed signals (latency + cost).
- Automation: scheduled rollback window + feature-flag adjust + automatic traffic sampler change.
- Owner: Release steward + SRE-runner for capacity checks.

Level 2 — Full rollback / immediate stop (higher impact):
- Action: Disable experiment route entirely and revert model version. Engage postmortem comms.
- Trigger: Safety regression OR quality drop beyond agreed SLA OR silent failure.
- Automation: feature flag toggle that immediately fingers off traffic, followed by automated cutover to baseline.
- Owner: Release lead + oncall + product PM.

Level 3 — Escalation to incident (exec + customer comms):
- Action: Declare incident, open incident channel, run incident runbook, notify customer success for impacted customers.
- Trigger: large-scale user harm, regulatory exposure, or inability to remediate in 30 minutes.
- Owner: Incident commander (SRE + Product lead).

Mapping examples (mini playbooks):
1) Latency inflation observed in EU cohort after deploying prompt-X variation:
- Detect: latency.p95_eu >= baseline +300ms sustained 12m.
- Automated first step: soft mitigation (route new EU sessions to baseline) — automated via router.
- If persists 15m: throttle exposure (2% cap) + run autoscaling sanity check.
- If persists 30m: full rollback for EU.
- Notes: run a quick A/B-check with synthetic load to validate whether change is model-internal vs infra. Link: github simulation PR.

2) Rise in safety flags on search-summarize pipeline for specific query class:
- Detect: safety.flag_rate_session_type("summarize") > 3x baseline for 5m and flags cluster around same semantic tokens.
- Immediate: full rollback (Level 2) for that route, disable the transformer prompt module.
- Notify: legal/compliance + CS for customers likely impacted.
- Post-action: capture sample transcripts, attach to security ticket, run targeted evals with safe prompts.

3) Cost runaway in reranking variant during batch bursts:
- Detect: cost_per_token_experiment projected burn > 10% of reserved in 30m window.
- Action: throttle to baseline plus auto-enable caching for repeated prefixes; schedule slower mode for non-interactive flows.
- If still > 30m: snapshot traffic, full rollback.

Guidelines for thresholds (practical):
- Keep thresholds conservative for safety signals (low false negatives) and tolerate some sensitivity for latency; tune with simulation.
- Use rolling windows and min-request-count gating to avoid flip-flop on thin traffic.
- Maintain at least two orthogonal signals before hard rollback except for explicit safety policy hits.

Automation checklist (implementation notes):
- Feature flagging: support slice-level overrides via API + console with audit logs and TTL (so temporary overrides auto-unwind if left).
- Router APIs: stable idempotent endpoints for route_override + forced_baseline with quick convergence.
- Playbooks: script templates for each Level action (Slack templates, incident channel creation, PagerDuty notes).
- Synthetic probes: maintain a suite of synthetic scenarios per cohort (short, medium, long context) to reproduce latency and quality patterns.
- Snapshotting: when an alert triggers, capture representative request traces, model kv-cache snapshots (if privacy allows), and first N outputs.

Human-in-loop and comms templates (short):
- Slack: "[AUTO] Canary alert: safety.flag_rate for summarize-route exceeded 3x baseline in cohort EU. Soft-mitigated by routing new sessions to baseline. Owner: @LenaChen. Next step: decide throttle or rollback by 15:20 UTC."
- Email to CS: short template that includes impact cohort, start time, estimated affected users, and whether manual mitigation applied.

Simulation plan (to validate choreography):
- Create a test harness that can: run controlled synthetic traffic with variable query distributions; inject simulated model regressions (latency, hallucination probability, safety flags); automatically measure response to automated mitigations.
- Run matrix: exposure_percent in [1,5,10], degradation_magnitude in [mild, moderate, severe], windows [5m,15m,30m].
- Evaluate how often automation correctly chooses Level 0/1 vs escalates erroneously. Tune thresholds to minimize unnecessary Level 2 actions while preserving safety.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How to standardize semantic-drift measurement across model families and prompt engineering changes? (Lena to prototype embedding-distance thresholding.)
- What is the recommended TTL for auto-unwind feature flag overrides? (Default 1 hour? 15 mins?)
- How to safely snapshot token-level traces while honoring customer privacy and PII? (Security + Legal input needed.)
- Define canonical SLO deltas that trigger product-level notification (PM + Legal).

Next steps (near term):
- Prototype the router API hook and a TTLed feature-flag override (engineering: Miguel).
- Build simulator scaffolding and run first sweep for latency-only scenarios (Lena + SRE infra).
- Draft compliance-safe telemetry snapshot guide (Security + Legal).
- Align on comms templates and assign roster for release stewardship for next three cross-functional releases.

Appendix: quick reference table (operator cheat sheet)
- Safety flag spike (>=3x baseline, >=0.1% absolute): Level 2 rollback immediate, notify legal.
- Latency p95 +250ms for 10m: Level 0 soft route override, monitor 15m; escalate to Level 1 if no improvement.
- Cost >2x baseline for 15m: Level 0 switch caching, Level 1 throttle, Level 2 rollback if persists.
- Silent failure (5xx >0.5%): Level 2 immediate rollback.

Notes to self: this is intentionally procedural and checklist-like. We'll flatten into machine-readable playbook once thresholds are validated by simulation. Keep this doc as the canonical working notes for choreography planning.

History / edits:
- 2025-11-03: initial sketch (Asha)
- 2025-12-18: added decision ladder and example playbooks (Lena)
- 2026-02-10: simulation plan & thresholds draft (Miguel)

Action owners: Asha (doc steward), Miguel (automation prototype), Lena (sim harness), Priya (comms + CS liaison)
